project.name: FLAREX
project.challenge: Flame in Freefall: SI-Powered Fire Safety Insights from Microgravity Combustion Data

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II
investigations.platform: International Space Station; Microgravity Science Glovebox
investigations.purpose: Investigate solid-material flame behavior and extinction in microgravity under varying airflow and sample conditions.
reported_findings: Flames were sensitive to airflow speed in the 0–5 cm/s range in the reported tests.
Some flames could persist below 1 cm/s as dim blue stable flames; the supplied presentation notes that a sudden airflow increase could change their behavior.
investigations.limitations: The supplied source is a presentation/abstract, not a raw numerical dataset. Do not fabricate time series or chart values.

investigations.name: Saffire: A Novel Approach to Study of Spacecraft Fire Safety Using Unmanned Spacecraft
investigations.platform: Uncrewed Cygnus cargo spacecraft after departure from ISS
investigations.purpose: Study fire behavior at larger scales in an uncrewed spacecraft, separated from crewed vehicles.
reported_findings: The investigation examined whether flame growth would reach a steady size.
The enclosure size around a sample had more influence on flame spread than anticipated, according to the supplied summary.
investigations.limitations: The supplied source is a presentation abstract, not a raw dataset.

investigations.name: Operation and Development Status of the Spacecraft Fire Experiments (Saffire)
investigations.purpose: Demonstrate material flammability tests at realistic spacecraft fire length scales in low gravity.

sample_details.Saffire-I-and-III: Composite fabric approximately 0.4 m wide by 0.94 m long; 75% cotton and 25% fiberglass by mass; nominal cabin oxygen near 0.21 mole fraction.
sample_details.Saffire-II: Nine samples approximately 5 cm by 29 cm; materials included PMMA, silicone, composite fabric, and Nomex; examined low-gravity maximum oxygen concentration flammability limits.

diagnostics: inlet, flame-plume, and outlet temperature sensors
reported_findings: Camera images were primary diagnostics for Saffire-II propagation or self-extinction observations.
historical_notes: Saffire-I launched aboard Cygnus OA-6 on 2016-03-22; it berthed with ISS on 2016-03-25 and the test was initiated after unberthing.
A supplied 2016 paper described Saffire-IV/V/VI as planned follow-on work. Those plans must not be presented as proof of completion.
investigations.limitations: The source excerpt contains experiment descriptions and instrumentation, not a full raw numerical dataset. Historical plans must be labeled as plans.

investigations.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment / Reflight
investigations.purpose: Characterize smoke-particle size and morphology in low gravity to inform spacecraft smoke-detector development.

teams_and_roles.principal_investigator: Dr. David Urban, NASA Glenn Research Center
teams_and_roles.project_scientist: Dr. Gary Ruff, NASA Glenn Research Center

investigations.SAME_initial_goal: Quantitatively determine smoke particulate size from low-gravity sources to help define future detector requirements.
investigations.SAME_R_goal: Obtain particle morphology data, reduce uncertainty in size distributions, and compare SAME with earlier Shuttle experiments.
investigations.hardware_description: Reuse of SAME hardware with refurbished or new sample carousels and thermal precipitators plus a new diagnostics unit.
investigations.operations_summary: Crew setup and periodic consumable changes; autonomous operation using parameters uplinked from the ground.
investigations.limitations: The supplied slides do not provide numerical particle sizes or morphology values. Milestone dates in the slides are historical plans, not current schedule data.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.family: Liquid-droplet combustion and gaseous suppressant research
investigations.purpose: Study near-limit diffusion flames, liquid-fuel combustion, extinction, inert-gas suppressant effectiveness, and combustion-model validation in microgravity.

reported_experimental_ranges.suppressant_concentration: 0 to an expected limit near 0.70 for the least active suppressant, as described in supplied source

reported_topics: detailed and reduced-order model development and validation
investigations.limitations: Ranges are experimental variables, not universal safety thresholds or findings. Do not treat them as operational fire-suppression instructions.

investigations.name: FLEX-2, FLEX-2J, and FLEX-ICE-GA
investigations.purpose: Extend droplet-combustion research to more representative fuel mixtures, convective-flow effects, droplet arrays, and alternative fuels.

FLEX-2J: flame spread along one-dimensional droplet arrays
three fixed droplets and additional movable droplets described in supplied configuration
measurements include droplet motion, burning time, flame spread, spacing, pressure, and gas composition

investigations.limitations: Configuration descriptions and planned test group counts are not equivalent to measured results. Do not create synthetic experiment outcomes.

investigations.name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments
investigations.family: Gaseous diffusion flames and fundamental combustion
investigations.platform: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR), International Space Station
investigations.purpose: Investigate fundamental combustion in microgravity, including fuel-lean flames, soot, oxygen-enriched combustion, stability/extinction, electric-field effects, and model validation.
investigations.source_note: One supplied source paragraph says five experiments, while the detailed list names six. This file preserves the six detailed experiment names and flags the source inconsistency.

BRE.description: Flat porous burner supplied with gaseous fuel to emulate aspects of solid/liquid fuel burning; studies material flammability, ignition/extinction, and relevance of terrestrial tests.

CLD Flame.description: Studies sooty pure-fuel and highly diluted near-extinction flames.
reported_findings: In studied conditions, microgravity flames were taller, wider, cooler, and sootier than normal-gravity flames.

One supplied source reports soot volume fraction 5–8 times normal gravity in its studied conditions; another context mentions nearly a factor of ten. Keep these study-specific and do not merge them into one universal multiplier.

E-FIELD Flames.description: Studies how electric fields influence combustion-generated ions and potentially flame shape, soot, flammability limits, heat transfer, and emissions.
E-FIELD Flames.caveat: Electric-field simulation is not direct partial-gravity experimental data.

Flame Design.description: Studies soot inception/extinction, oxygen-enriched combustion, and spherical microgravity flames.

s-Flame.description: Studies spherical diffusion-flame structure, dynamics, extinction, soot-free and sooty flames; fuels listed include hydrogen, methane, and ethylene.

CFI-G.description: Studies quasi-steady spherical cool diffusion flames on a porous burner and cool-flame chemistry for model validation.
CFI-G.special_context: Challenge page supplied by user states the highest oxygen-concentration microgravity tests were ACME CFI-G, with chamber mixture nitrogen plus flammable gas and O2/N2 mixture up to 85% oxygen flowing from a spherical burner for an inside-out flame. Treat this as a specific configuration, not a general spacecraft atmosphere.

investigations.hardware_context: CIR insert and associated burners, igniter, gas-delivery system, and avionics. The challenge-page information maps six ACME experiments to the same modular ACME hardware in CIR.
investigations.limitations: Supplied information is descriptive and does not provide a complete numerical dataset. Do not expose high-voltage hardware operating instructions.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Combustion in Partial and Micro-Gravity
investigations.purpose: Review solid-fuel combustion physics and fire-safety knowledge gaps in microgravity and partial gravity.
high_level_physics: Diffusion, radiation, material properties, geometry, and imposed airflow can become comparatively important.
Material heating and pyrolysis influence subsequent combustion behavior.
review_observations: BASS/BASS-II and Saffire findings indicate that material, geometry, scale, and flow conditions matter.
Some reported Saffire tests observed continued combustion-related activity after a temporary flow change; this is specific to those tests and not a universal rule.
Partial-gravity evidence is limited; some studies suggest gravity level can influence concurrent-flow spread, but findings should be presented with uncertainty.
research_gaps: coupled solid/gas heat and mass transfer
material deformation, charring, cracking, and swelling
battery thermal runaway, cooling, energy release, and gas hazards
investigations.limitations: This is a review, not a single experiment dataset. Avoid turning its discussion into operational fire-management advice.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.purpose: Verify a modified ultrafine particle counter in microgravity and assess its suitability for future spacecraft aerosol and smoke measurements.
investigations.instrument_description: Modified P-Trak ultrafine particle counter; supplied description says it uses condensation of isopropyl alcohol vapor on particles to enable optical detection.
investigations.relationship_to_other_investigations: Risk-reduction work related to SAME; SAME intended to measure particles in an approximate 0.2–1 micron range, according to supplied notes.
reported_observations: Supplied summary reports low particulate levels aboard ISS relative to Shuttle and larger average particle sizes on orbit than on Earth; proposed explanations are tentative and should not be stated as proven causes.
investigations.limitations: The supplied record is a description/results summary, not a complete raw dataset. Do not provide instrument construction or operating instructions.

investigations.name: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
investigations.hardware: SPICE hardware, based on ELF hardware
investigations.purpose: Study laminar diffusion flame structure and flame liftoff/stabilization in microgravity.
objectives: characterize flame structure and attached/lifted states
study liftoff behavior in relation to fuel and burner diameter
support comparison of imagery with numerical models
investigations.relationship: SLICE was a precursor to CLD Flame and provided preliminary research; SPICE and SLICE share hardware, while SPICE focuses on soot/smoke-point behavior.
investigations.limitations: Supplied record describes objectives and observations, not full numerical data. No flame-test instructions.

investigations.name: Smoke Point in Co-flow Experiment
investigations.purpose: Study smoke point, soot formation and oxidation, flame shape, stabilization height, temperature field, and soot emission in non-buoyant jet diffusion flames.
investigations.relationship: SPICE and SLICE use the same hardware; SPICE emphasizes soot/smoke-point research, while SLICE emphasizes flame structure and liftoff.
investigations.limitations: The supplied source summary gives counts but no full numerical measurements or raw dataset.

investigations.name: Fire and Gas Characterization Studies for Lithium-ion Cells and Batteries
investigations.source: Underwriters Laboratories presentation at 2020 NASA Aerospace Battery Workshop
investigations.purpose: Characterize fire hazards, vent gases, and smoke for selected LFP and NMC cells, modules, and batteries.
investigations.test_context: The supplied presentation compared selected LFP cylindrical and NMC prismatic configurations at 100% state of charge using a UL 9540A heating profile.
reported_specific_test_observations: In the described tests, NMC modules/battery showed propagation with fire; LFP modules/battery showed thermal-runaway propagation without external flaming in the reported cases.
The presentation reports example maximum temperatures of 1459°C for an NMC battery and 661°C for an LFP battery; these are test-specific, not universal chemistry properties.
Single-cell gas sample volumes and gas compositions differed in the reported tests, but cell capacities/configurations differ, so direct chemistry-only comparisons are not justified.
key_caveats: Thermal runaway and visible external fire are not synonymous.
Single-cell tests cannot alone predict module or pack behavior.
Configuration and heat-transfer pathways affect outcomes.
This is not microgravity or ISS data.
investigations.limitations: Use only as clearly labeled complementary terrestrial battery-hazard context. Do not mix it into microgravity dataset charts or imply NASA performed these UL tests.

investigations.name: Confined Combustion
investigations.purpose: Study flame spread through differently shaped confined spaces and the influence of wall radiation and geometry in microgravity.
investigations.historical_note: NASA overview says the first burn was performed by Christina Koch on Christmas Eve 2019.
investigations.limitations: User supplied a NASA overview, not the full paper or raw data. No numerical spread rates or geometry-specific measurements are available in the notes. SoFIE-OFFS is a separate investigation.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction – Oscillatory Flow on Flame Spread
investigations.family: Solid-fuel flame spread under non-steady flow
investigations.platform: ISS; SoFIE and Combustion Integrated Rack
investigations.purpose: Study transient flame motion and flame spread through fine fuels under non-steady concurrent airflow, with relevance to wildfire behavior and spacecraft fire safety.
investigations.approach: Controlled non-steady forced flow is used to study flame response in microgravity, where buoyancy-driven flow is absent.
reported_context: The NASA entry describes approximately 30 experiments.
The investigation explores how transient flame motion affects convective heating and ignition of fine fuels.
investigations.limitations: The supplied NASA entry describes objectives and methods but not numerical results/raw data. Treat the listed period and experiment count as source metadata, not a claim that all results are available.

investigations.principal_investigator: Carlos Fernandez-Pello, University of California, Berkeley
investigations.platform: ISS; SoFIE and Combustion Integrated Rack
investigations.purpose: Study thermally assisted burning and ignition/extinction boundaries for solid fuel in microgravity under varying environmental conditions.
investigations.sample_description: PMMA cylinder solid-fuel samples, as described in the supplied NASA entry.

hardware_mapping.ACME: Six ACME investigations use common modular ACME hardware in CIR, according to supplied challenge page.
hardware_mapping.FLEX_FLEX2_CFI: FLEX, FLEX-2, and CFI use MDCA in CIR, according to supplied challenge page.
hardware_mapping.BASS_BASS2_SPICE_SLICE: BASS, BASS-II, SPICE, and SLICE use MSG with a modular fan-driven flow duct developed for SPICE, according to supplied challenge page.

atmosphere_context.spacesuit: 100% oxygen at 4.3 psi, as stated in the supplied challenge page.
atmosphere_context.earth_sea_level: 14.7 psi, as stated in the supplied challenge page.
atmosphere_context.moon_base_or_pressurized_rover: Challenge page describes candidate contexts with oxygen at or above 30% and pressure at or below 10.2 psi.
atmosphere_context.cfi_g: Challenge page states CFI-G included a nitrogen/flammable-gas chamber mixture and oxygen/nitrogen mixture up to 85% oxygen in a specific experimental configuration.

challenge_context.partial_gravity_caveat: No direct partial-gravity combustion dataset was described as currently available in PSI in the supplied challenge page. Future LUCI and FM2 may add data. E-FIELD Flames simulate certain effects using electric fields and are not direct lunar/Martian gravity experiments.
challenge_context.scope_exclusion: Rocket and propellant fires are outside the stated challenge scope.
challenge_context.important_note: These values and statements are captured from the user-provided challenge-page text. Recheck the official challenge source before treating them as independently verified facts.

data_quality_rules: Every displayed fact must carry a source label and URL.
Do not display a numeric chart unless source-backed numeric values exist.
A source's experiment range is not automatically a result, safety limit, or recommendation.
A review paper is not an experiment dataset.
A NASA investigation description is not raw PSI data.
The UL lithium-ion battery presentation is complementary terrestrial research, not microgravity/ISS data.
Distinguish Saffire historical plans from completed investigations.
Do not claim direct partial-gravity measurements based on E-FIELD Flames.
Do not merge different study-specific soot multipliers into a single universal value.
Do not treat planned experiment counts as completed test counts.
